newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PM says Bangladesh offered $700 mln in investment.
newsitem.headline: PM says Bangladesh offered $700 mln in investment.

text.p: Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said on Sunday that foreign investors had offered 30 billion taka ($700 million) to Bangladesh, and appealed to opposition politicial parties to maintain national stability.

"We have got huge investment offers. We could draw the attention of foreign investors in a short time. Now the opposition should not do anything that might destabilise the investment climate," newspapers on Monday quoted her as telling a rally in southwestern Jessore town.
"Political stability is a must for economic development, and all should try their best to ensure that," said Hasina, who took office last June after her Awami League won general elections.
Hasina's appeal came amid threats by her political rival, former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia, to wage a massive anti-government movement.

The executive committee of Khaleda's Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) decided on Sunday to begin a nationwide agitation soon to protest what a party leader called the "repressive and undemocratic" attitude of the ruling party.
Khaleda was expected to announce the agitation programme on Wednesday at a public rally in southeastern Feni district, her constituency, the BNP leader said.
Violent street protests by opposition parties in recent years against the former BNP government seriously hurt business in Bangladesh and drove away prospective foreign investors.
Bangladesh started receiving significant investment offers, particualrly from international oil and energy firms, when stability returned after the June elections.
